current_finding: Canonical SWAP5 remains without an admitted solute owner or salinity response. This work branch adds independently testable local prototypes for conservative mobile salt mass with explicit upwind advection, the Maas-Hoffman response, and a continuity-based reconstruction of interval-mean internal water face fluxes from accepted start/end storage and signed node sources. The reconstruction is manufactured-tested and checked against a real single-solve Reference Richards case with nonzero subsurface source and separately bound nonzero root sink. The broader live serialized FMR A8 transaction suite now passes at O0/O2 after fixture-local matrix_area_fraction repair; its A7 case accepts nonzero qrot with closed transactional water mass and passes discard/replay/restart. A restricted live FMR producer now emits ordered water/source/sink and boundary-flux records for each accepted Richards physical substep. The trace is trial observation data, is discarded on rejected attempts, and is fail-closed on unsupported routes; A7 validates both accepted halfsteps, nodewise continuity, exact nonzero qrot, discard/replay and changed-forcing restart replay. It does not yet bind salt transport to FMR or represent the excluded special routes. Salt state remains unbound to transaction/restart and omits dispersion, solute substeps and boundary-schedule integration. Jarvis remains fail-closed for salinity. Added a falsifiable transport boundary: an interval-mean continuity flux cannot identify gross or ordered advective transport under within-interval reversal, so it remains diagnostic-only. The physics test now includes an executable reversal counterexample showing equal/opposite half-step water fluxes yield zero signed mean but nonzero ordered donor-concentration salt transfer. Checked the official SWAP release path: it advertises SWAP 4.3.1 development release but exposes a registration form, not an accessible source archive in this execution. Exact B1.11 solute source remains unavailable here. Exact B0/B1.11 member identity for SWAP/solute.f90 is known from the local manifest (SHA-256 2fc8592001cdcd2de95a252d8b9099416c94e4d2654c335908858a735f80e7a2; 51,508 bytes); B1.11 SWAP-011 does not modify that member. The raw bytes remain unavailable for semantic reconstruction. Direct bounds-checked GNU Fortran O0 builds passed for the mobile salt state, salinity response, and face-flux reconstruction unit tests; the face test includes the within-interval reversal counterexample. These remain local prequalification, not production qualification. Corrected source availability: a Git-backed solute source does exist at SWAP-model/SWAP@c22bd832ddf3e53e330a552f5e31e74f183362d1. It is a v4.2.0-derived modular source and fails the pinned B1.11 member hash/size check, so it is now used only for corroborative algorithm review; the prior claim that no Git solute source was available was too broad.
historical_reconstruction: Source-family evidence distinguishes Maas-Hoffman switch 1 as a nodewise alpha(CML) from osmotic-head switch 2, which modifies matric-flux potential and requires Jong-van-Lier drought; switch 2 is not a separate multiplicative alpha_sol. Source-family census additionally establishes SWINCO-dependent initial versus warm-restart concentration profiles, CMSY inventory derived from water content/CML and optional Freundlich sorption, explicit boundary and drainage fluxes, internal solute substeps, and root salt uptake TSCF*qrot*CML. Exact B1.11 solute-member and restart details remain unverified in this execution.

Canonical runtime/restart has no salt-state owner; the current module is a pure trial transformation and is not an accepted production transaction.

FMR represents optional physical continuations through explicit clone families and template-layout cases. A salinity state must define coexistence with these families and preserve salinity-disabled layouts before changing production state interfaces.

Prototype is explicit advective upwind only, with no dispersive flux, internal timestep substeps, drainage, boundary schedule, or restart serialization. These remain separate physical/numerical acceptance gates.

FMR now exposes an accepted ordered water/source/sink substep trace for a restricted Richards route; it is not connected to the salt process and special surface/snow/drainage/macropore routes remain unsupported or unqualified.

The interval-mean reconstruction remains diagnostic for salinity transport under within-interval reversal; the new ordered trace resolves this only for the restricted live FMR route and must be preserved transactionally when a salt consumer is added.

The Git-backed SWAP-model/SWAP solute source has been retrieved and hashed, but it does not match the pinned B1.11 member identity (18,271 bytes / 85fc… versus 51,508 bytes / 2fc859…). Do not claim exact B1.11 source equivalence; continue provisional source-family implementation and preserve the identity gap until a matching Git object is located or the B1.11 member is otherwise recovered.
recovery_point: PPA-WU05-E has restricted E1 and E2 local prototypes on the work branch. Focused O0/O2 salinity tests pass, including a manufactured and restricted real-Reference-Richards conservative internal water-face-flux reconstruction. The direct solve includes nonzero qssdi and separately bound nonzero qrot. The A8 O0/O2 FMR transaction/restart suite now passes with nonzero qrot, after correcting incomplete test-only matrix_area_fraction configuration. However the FMR observation does not expose interval-aggregated boundary fluxes or accepted-substep traces, so continuity reconstruction is not connected to FMR and live solute transport is not qualified. A source-backed transaction/restart audit establishes that kernel commit and Restart v2 each own one physical state object and that FMR restart layout is explicitly discriminated. The branch has selected an optional typed salt component plus an independent template/restart layout identity; this design is proposed, not canonically accepted or implemented. No Jarvis interface was changed and no salinity capability is qualified/admitted. Exact B1.11 solute-member bytes, common-state/clone/restart implementation, and live accepted-substep transport binding remain open. At checkpoint 0d83f16819f3bbe6d1a97481252d842fbe2aed86, `advance_mobile_salt_trace` and exact O0/O2 reversal, water continuity, late-failure rollback, and deterministic retry/restart replay tests are added; the branch runner passes. This API is not wired to FMR, and salinity remains unqualified.

source_family_census.initialization: SWINCO != 3 interpolates ZC/CML input to nodes; SWINCO = 3 consumes a warm-start concentration profile and does not reapply the initial table (source-family only).
source_family_census.state: CML is mobile-water concentration; CMSY is dissolved plus adsorbed mass per bulk soil volume; column inventory integrates CMSY over node thickness.
source_family_census.transport: Surface input, inter-node advective/dispersive flux, bottom exchange, lateral drainage, root uptake, optional decomposition; internal solute substeps.
source_family_census.root_salt_uptake: TSCF*qrot*CML is a solute-mass sink; must use the same candidate/accepted qrot as the one root-water sink.
source_family_census.ownership: Dedicated solute-state owner advances candidate salt mass and commits/rolls it back with the physical transaction; Jarvis reads concentration only.
source_family_census.exact_source_limit: All equations and lifecycle details above are source-family corroboration only, not byte-exact B1.11 claims.

initial_e1_envelope: One conservative dissolved salt constituent in mobile water; SWSP=0; decomposition, macropore, ageing, aquifer mixing, MICRO and lateral drainage off; explicit top/bottom solute boundary traces; root salt uptake through TSCF*qrot*CML with restricted 0<=TSCF<=1; node salt mass authoritative, CML derived from matching committed/trial water content; paired water/salt trial commit/discard.
